headline: Oil runs toward $105–$110 as NATO–Russia fears collapse; Brazil votes tomorrow
summary: The Russia–Ukraine meeting happened, and NATO–Russia clash odds collapsed from 20% to 2% for October. Oil kept climbing: $105 this month is now 78%. Large traders put about $225k on the Fed holding next week. Apple is suddenly a real threat to pass Nvidia by month-end. Brazil's runoff is tomorrow, with Bolsonaro near 80%.

takeaways.text: WTI reaching $105 this month jumped 22 pts in a day to 78% (up 34 this week). $110 is 34% (up 9), and even $115 is 11.6% (up 4). A drop back to $95 fell 12 pts to 25%. An all-time high by March rose to 25.5%.

takeaways.lead: NATO–Russia fears collapsed after the meeting.
takeaways.text: The Russia–Ukraine meeting happened (that market is at 100%, with $109k of large bets at the finish). A NATO–Russia military clash by Oct 31 crashed 18 pts to 2.2%, and by year-end fell 18 to 18.5% ($12M market). The next talks are expected in the UAE (67%), with Switzerland rising 15 pts to 20% (thin market). Peace talks by year-end are 82.5%.

takeaways.lead: $225k bet the Fed holds next week.
takeaways.text: One trader put $151k on no change at the Oct 29 meeting, and another $76k went against a hike. No change is 93.5%. A December hike is still 74%, with a $9k bet added on it.

takeaways.lead: Apple might pass Nvidia by month-end.
takeaways.text: Apple as the largest company at the end of October jumped 16 pts in a day to 38% (up 19 this week), and Nvidia fell 17 to 60.5% (thin $813k market). Google is now 92% to have the best AI model at month-end, and Anthropic is down to 6.5%.

takeaways.lead: Brazil votes tomorrow, and Bolsonaro is near 80%.
takeaways.text: Flávio Bolsonaro rose 3 pts to 79.9%, and Lula fell 2 to 20%. A Bolsonaro win by 4–8 points rose 6 to 35%, and under 4 points is 39.5%. Large bets: about $80k on Bolsonaro's side and $15k on Lula's. Watch the Brazilian real and the EWZ fund on Monday.

takeaways.lead: Overlooked: Israel may close its airspace (thin).
takeaways.text: Israel closing its airspace (excluding holidays) by year-end jumped 11 pts to 37.5% (thin $530k market, up 13 this week). That's usually a sign traders expect Iranian strikes. The Israel–Iran ceasefire through Nov 15 is only 56.5% (down 11 this week).

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: Anthropic's IPO timing slipped: by Nov 30 fell 13 pts to 59.5%, and by Nov 25 fell 23 to 45.5%. By year-end is still 78.5%.
Serbia: Vučić's party winning the most seats rose to 71.5% (up 11 this week), with about $132k of large bets on it.
Bulgaria: Iliana Iotova is the clear favorite for president (a $22k bet at 88¢); winning the first round by 10–20 points is 60.5%.

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Oil: $105 this month 78%, $110 34%, $115 11.6%. Energy is the strongest trend on the page.
Rates: Fed hold 93.5%, December hike 74%. Canada hikes Oct 28 (81%). The 10-year yield reaching 5.5% this year fell 8 pts to 9.5%, so bond fears are fading.
Tech: Apple vs Nvidia at month-end is now a real race (38% vs 60.5%).
Anthropic's IPO is likely by year-end (78.5%) but probably not before late November.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: NATO–Russia clash by year-end: 18.5% (down 18 in a day). The biggest de-escalation of the week.
US–Iran ceasefire through Oct 31: 79% (up 2); through Oct 28: 87% (up 5).
A Saudi–Houthi ceasefire by year-end fell 12 pts to 18.5% (thin market). Saudi airspace closing by year-end fell 7 to 17.5%.

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Brazil (tomorrow, Oct 25): Bolsonaro 79.9%, Lula 20%. The closest outcomes (either side winning by under 4 points) are 57% combined.
Israel (Oct 27): Eizenkot 51.4% (up 2), Netanyahu 26.5% (down 2). Large traders bet about $40k against Netanyahu.
US midterms (Nov 3): Democratic sweep 66.5%, Republican Senate with Democratic House 24.5%. A $32k long-shot bet went on Republicans holding the House (Democrats take the House 91.5%).

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Gas: oil is likely to hit $105 this month. Expect pump prices to keep rising into early November.
US borrowing: the Fed holds next week (93.5%), but a December hike is still likely (74%).
Canadian borrowers: a hike on Wednesday is 81% likely.
